highlights.title: Gateway-mediated OpenClaw security path through protected audit timeline
highlights.description: The cumulative local snapshot adds the isolated OpenClaw agent path, capability and policy boundaries, approval, bidirectional model mediation, authoritative effect readback, receipts, and the protected audit timeline.

highlights.title: Mechanism-independent Agent Runtime Isolation contract
highlights.description: Canon and Zoo guidance now distinguish the untrusted runtime contract from any single Docker reference adapter and state the exact local claim boundary.

highlights.title: Evidence-first README and low-friction contribution path
highlights.description: The README uses strict maturity classes, knowledge positioning, system connection guidance, and issue-to-release traceability without turning roadmap issues into evidence.

highlights.title: Deterministic non-publishing Daily POC candidate
highlights.description: One manifest now drives release notes, evidence indexes, reproducible candidate bytes, and the update-video facts while publication remains outside the pipeline.

useCases.title: Mediate model requests and responses in both directions

claims.statement: The isolated OpenClaw fixture has no ambient provider, host, or tenant credential and reaches the declared application path only through the ChimpMaera Gateway boundary.

nonClaims.statement: This local Docker fixture is not a hostile-host, kernel, hypervisor, or production sandbox claim.

claims.statement: The local model broker guards requests before provider access and guards responses before agent or tool use while credentials remain opaque to the agent.

nonClaims.statement: No live-provider, universal-agent, production TLS, DNS, or vault behavior is claimed.

claims.statement: In the synthetic governed path, transport acceptance is not success; authoritative readback and a bound receipt are required after effect-boundary enforcement.

nonClaims.statement: No production provider transaction, ETag, IAM, MFA, quorum, revoke, or rollback service is claimed.

claims.statement: Verified audit explanations require signed ordered digest-linked facts plus the exact head and count checkpoint; tampered, missing, reordered, or forked facts do not render verified success.

nonClaims.statement: No hostile-host tamper-proof store, independent witness, trusted time, production key custody, or retention compliance is claimed.

claims.statement: The local Canon revision defines a mechanism-independent untrusted runtime contract and separates it from the Docker reference adapter.

nonClaims.statement: VM, MicroVM, WASM, remote-worker, Hermes, and Claude Code runtime compatibility remain unproven here.

claims.statement: The contribution guide distinguishes planning, readiness, implementation, local validation, merge, and public-delivery states and treats issues as roadmap rather than evidence.

nonClaims.statement: This candidate does not close or silently advance any public issue.

claims.statement: The Daily POC compiler produces deterministic evidence-bound candidate artifacts from one manifest and a clean frozen source while keeping public effects disabled.

nonClaims.statement: Candidate preparation grants no merge, tag, release, upload, or deployment authority.

knownLimitations: This is a local synthetic POC candidate, not a production deployment or security certification.
LOCALLY VALIDATED is not RELEASED; PLANNED is not PROVEN.
The OpenClaw, model-broker, effect, readback, receipt, and audit evidence is bounded to the exact local fixtures and threat model.
BLD-001, AAS-038, AAS-039, BI and DMS expansion, and unfinished evergreen video work are outside this snapshot.
Issues #2 through #8 remain roadmap and traceability links; no issue closes before merge.
The update video is rendered and checked locally under a separate non-publishing production step.
externalGates: The review pull request must receive its GitHub PR number and CI result after the green local gate.
Merge, tag, prerelease, stable release, deployment, and README publication require separate Owner action.
YouTube upload requires a separate Owner-authorized publication step.
Production, customer, live-provider, and independent hostile-host evidence require external validation.

segments.title: Snapshot status
segments.purpose: Name the exact candidate and distinguish local validation from public delivery.
segments.narration: This is ChimpMaera Daily POC candidate v0.2.0-poc.20260801.1. It combines the completed local product and security slices through AAS-023 into one reviewable snapshot. The evidence is bound to this local candidate; public delivery is a separate gate.
visuals: Show the candidate version and frozen public-main-to-candidate source range.
Show four status labels: proven here, locally validated, planned, and external gate.

segments.title: OpenClaw without ambient authority
segments.purpose: Explain the untrusted runtime and Gateway-only application path.
segments.narration: A real OpenClaw agent fixture runs as untrusted workload code. It receives no ambient provider, host, or tenant credential. The declared application path goes through the ChimpMaera Gateway, while direct provider, peer, socket, host, and unmanaged effect paths remain denied in the tested fixture.
visuals: Place OpenClaw inside the untrusted runtime boundary.
Show one outbound Gateway path and crossed-out ambient authority paths.

segments.title: Capability is not authority
segments.purpose: Show the policy and approval chain before any effect.
segments.narration: A capability is only something the system could do. Runtime authority stays inactive until scope, policy generation, exact plan, human-readable diff, and approval all bind to the same action. Trusted code rechecks those facts at use time, outside the agent, and ambiguity fails closed.
visuals: Animate Capability to Policy to Plan and Diff to Approval to use-time Gate.
Keep the agent visually outside every trusted decision box.

segments.title: Bidirectional model broker
segments.purpose: Show request and response mediation around the provider.
segments.narration: Model access is bidirectional and mediated. Requests are guarded before provider access; opaque credentials resolve only inside the broker. Responses and streams are guarded again before they return to the agent or a tool path. Model output remains untrusted data, never effect authority.
visuals: Animate guarded request traffic from agent to broker to provider.
Animate guarded response traffic back through the broker with a data-not-authority label.

segments.title: Effect, readback, and receipt
segments.purpose: Explain why transport acceptance is not success.
segments.narration: The bounded effect gate executes the exact approved action. A successful transport response is not enough. ChimpMaera queries the authoritative provider state, compares the material result, and only then binds the decision, effect, readback digest, and outcome into a receipt. Drift, replay, rejection, or ambiguity cannot become success.
visuals: Show the effect gate calling the synthetic system of record.
Return readback to a receipt card with a verified outcome; route failure states to denied.

segments.title: Audit timeline and honest boundaries
segments.purpose: Close with protected audit facts and separate proven, local, planned, and external states.
segments.narration: The protected audit timeline explains outcomes only from signed, ordered, digest-linked facts and the exact checkpoint. Missing, reordered, forked, or tampered facts do not render verified success. In this snapshot, the local contracts and tests are proven here, the isolated runtime evidence remains local, Builder Agent and broader integrations remain planned, and production or hostile-host claims remain external gates.
visuals: Build a signed audit timeline ending at an exact head and count checkpoint.
Close on four maturity columns with Builder Agent under planned and production under external gate.
